answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate and 14-day renewal deadline create pressure, but the 94% line utilization leaves zero margin for delivery failure. Memory_c4 demonstrates that renegotiating at renewal can recover real margin through benchmarking—this is the highest-probability path to the cost target without switching. Memory_c2 warns that the low-cost vendor is unreliable for critical lines (3 of 4 quarters missed SLA), making a switch to them unacceptable given current capacity constraints. Memory_c1 shows incumbent renewal preserves stability; memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing. Negotiate_terms preserves both cost ambition and delivery safety: benchmark the incumbent aggressively against the market, offer a 2-3 year commitment in exchange for the 18% reduction, and secure SLA protections. This buys time for next cycle to add a second source (memory_c3 path) if needed. If negotiation fails to reach 18%, defer has protected us before (memory_c5), though the non-renewable deadline here limits that option. Standard_experiment scope reflects measured urgency without recklessness. Flagging downstream risk because the cost target is aggressive and any vendor change carries execution risk at 94% utilization. Uncertainty preserved: negotiation outcome is not guaranteed; second-source option remains open for next cycle.
